function: Heterogeneous GNN jointly outputs BS beamforming matrix, RIS phase configurations and user-RIS association to maximize weighted sum rate (pp. 5-7).
system: Downlink mmWave: BS with Nt=8 antennas, 2 single-antenna users, 2 reflecting RISs of 16 elements (UPA), unit-modulus phases, direct links blocked; carrier frequency not stated (pp. 3, 9).
method: Heterogeneous GNN with message-passing MLPs; WSR loss (label-free) plus cross-entropy loss on nearest-RIS labels, pre-training sets the loss weight; Adam, 400 epochs (pp. 5-9).
data_channel: Simulated Saleh-Valenzuela mmWave channels (3 paths, 1 LoS), path loss with 5.8 dB shadowing; 110,000 samples; random user positions (p. 9).
test_conditions: Each SNR point trained and tested separately (p. 9); same 100,000/10,000 sample split; Nt and M varied in Figs. 9-10 without stated transfer (pp. 9, 11-12).
baselines: Non-learned: WMMSE with random phases, AO (WMMSE plus Riemannian conjugate gradient); learned: DNN with encoder-processing-decoder; GNN variants with predefined RIS association (pp. 9-11).
metrics: Weighted sum rate versus Pmax, M and Nt; running time (Table II); parameter count; testing WSR versus epochs and samples (pp. 11-13).
complexity: Measured running time of the GNN 0.050-0.054 s on CPU, 0.022-0.024 s on GPU (Table II); about 5.8 million parameters (p. 12).
q1_support: p. 4: "we consider the typical Saleh-Valenzuela" mmWave channel model. Not met: custom simulator with 3 paths and a log-distance path loss with shadowing (p. 9); no 3GPP, QuaDRiGa, COST 2100 or DeepMIMO model and no measured data.
q2_support: p. 9: "separately for each SNR point to evaluate its performance" (trained and tested per SNR point). Not met: Nt and M are varied in Figs. 9-10 without saying a trained model is reused, and K=2 users and R=2 RISs stay fixed (Table I).
q3_support: p. 10: "Benchmark 2 (AO): The AO algorithm is utilized as" and Benchmark 1 WMMSE with random phases (non-learned); p. 10: "Benchmark 3 (Intelligent DNN): To validate the" advantages of message passing. WSR curves in Figs. 7-8 (p. 11).
q4_support: p. 12: "GNN comprises roughly 5.8 million parameters, a moderate" count; Table II (p. 12) lists measured running times on CPU and GPU against the AO algorithm.
q5_support: p. 9: "split into 100,000 for training and 10,000 for validation, are" generated by the authors' own simulation. Not met: no link to code or data, no public dataset and no measured data anywhere in the paper (pp. 1-15).
notes: Included, area 3: the GNN outputs BS beamforming, RIS phases and user-RIS association (pp. 5-7); the association is learned jointly with the PHY variables, so the above-PHY exclusion does not apply. q1: path-loss constants (61.4, 2, 5.8 dB) come from [9] and the Saleh-Valenzuela model from [48], but the paper never says it uses NYUSIM or measured data; reviewer to confirm. q3 rests on the fully connected DNN benchmark plus AO and WMMSE with random phases; Cases 1-3 with the GNN are variants of the method. Tables I and II were read from PDF images (pp. 9, 12).
